It combines a deterministic front end for metadata extraction and bridge generation, structured translation prompts, numerical validation, and profiling-guided feedback to identify inefficient execution patterns. The bridge handles array-layout conversion separately from scientific computation. We evaluate LAFT using the Kessler warm-rain microphysics scheme and four LLMs: Claude, GPT, Gemini, and Qwen. All four validated translations reproduce the Fortran reference outputs to near floating-point precision for the evaluated case, but their GPU performance differs substantially with execution design. The Gemini-generated implementation achieves up to a 357-fold speedup over serial Fortran in cached execution at 1,000,000 atmospheric columns, excluding compilation and host-device transfers. The results demonstrate that numerical agreement alone does not ensure efficient GPU execution and motivate combining numerical validation with hardware-aware performance analysis. LAFT provides a practical workflow for modernizing legacy atmospheric physics code through LLM-assisted translation, deterministic interface generation, automated validation and repair, and reproducible profiling.

papers.title: From Prototype to Massing: Learning Graph Correspondence for Scalable Facade Modeling
papers.abstract: Facade articulation at building scale is usually resolved manually or through parametric systems that encode design intent as explicit rules. This paper investigates a complementary workflow in which a designer-authored prototype supplies transferable articulation logic. Prototype and target massing are represented as heterogeneous attributed graphs, and a Siamese graph attention network with instance-local triplet supervision embeds their segments in a shared metric space. Many-to-one nearest-neighbor retrieval then routes prototype Patterns to the larger target. On the original 85/15 within-corpus holdout, prototype-to-massing top-1 accuracy reached 96.5%, compared with a reported 76.5% raw-feature baseline. A Rhino demonstrator converts predicted correspondence into reusable facade Patterns, and qualitative applications on four built projects show the workflow across distinct massing organizations. The contribution is not automated facade generation, but an authoring model in which resolved geometry serves as a computational specification for project-scale propagation.

papers.title: Spectral optimization of spherical lattices and applications to classical and quantum interacting spin systems
papers.abstract: We develop an optimization algorithm for spherical lattice discretizations based on the spectrum of the discretized Laplace operator. Starting from refined icosahedral lattices, we minimize the splitting of the $(2\ell+1)$, $\ell=0,1,2,\dots$, continuum multiplets expected from $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ symmetry via gradient descent. This approach simultaneously produces lattices based on triangles with nearly uniform circumradii and perimeters. Although the optimization uses only the free-particle spectrum, we show that the resulting lattices carry over to interacting models. On the optimized lattices, rotational symmetry is restored for the critical Ising and Potts models and primary scaling dimensions are accurately reproduced for the three-dimensional Ising conformal field theory, when appropriate geometry-dependent interaction strengths are used. Higher-angular-momentum descendant states reveal weak residual symmetry breaking beyond the sectors protected by the underlying icosahedral symmetry.

papers.title: A Catalytic Algorithm for Transposing Unknown Qutrit Unitaries with Tight Query Bounds
papers.abstract: We construct exact deterministic circuits for transposing and inverting an unknown qutrit unitary $U\in\mathrm{SU}(3)$ using only forward queries. Three queries prepare a catalyst independently of the input state. Four further queries implement transposition while returning the catalyst unchanged and uncorrelated with the output. Two uses within an antisymmetric encoding implement inversion with eight processing queries and return the same catalyst. Reusing the catalyst implements $m$ transpositions or inversions with $3+4m$ or $3+8m$ total queries, respectively. More generally, we prove that exact transposition and inversion of an unknown $U\in\mathrm{SU}(d)$, $d\ge2$, require at least $d+1$ and $d^2-1$ processing queries, respectively, in fixed causal order. These processing bounds hold for any program state prepared independently of the input state using finitely many forward queries, even if that state is consumed during processing. Both our catalytic qutrit algorithms attain their respective bounds. Moreover, exact qutrit transposition with four processing queries requires at least three preparation queries, and our construction attains this bound.

papers.title: On the 100% Rule of Linear Programming
papers.abstract: The so-called ``100% rule'' is a somewhat classical and yet somehow obscure rule that gives some local sensitivity-analysis information based on the very limited local sensitivity-analysis information that is often made available by linear-programming software, derived from an optimal basis that is hidden from the user. Introduced in a classic undergraduate textbook in 1977, half a century ago, it was only picked up on by researchers in a very limited way, and while it appears in some undergraduate textbooks, it tends not to appear in most modern graduate-level textbooks. Our contributions are to celebrate and revive interest in the 100% rule and to extend it in a meaningful way. We introduce a cone rule that certifies primal feasibility for more right-hand sides than the 100% rule does, using the same information, and that can be applied in linear time. We then study when this cone rule is tight, that is, when it captures the entire cone of right-hand sides for which the basis remains feasible. We characterize tightness in every dimension for right-hand sides interior to that cone, make the characterization explicit for m=2 and m=3, and settle the question for tridiagonal bases in every dimension: tightness is impossible once m>=4, and for m=3 we give an explicit criterion in the entries of the basis. We give further results for symmetric, integer and unimodular bases. Finally, when tightness fails, we measure the fraction of the feasibility cone captured by the rule using normalized solid angles. For the autoregressive family at m=3, we obtain a closed-form candidate for the infimum of this fraction over all right-hand sides, whose optimality is supported numerically. We also obtain a closed-form expression for the best case over most of the correlation range, subject to two numerically verified properties, and estimate the best-case value numerically more generally.

papers.title: Incremental Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Human-in-the-Loop Decision Support
papers.abstract: We introduce iRAG, a human-in-the-loop decision-support system combining Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with Hybrid Decision-Making. Unlike conventional RAG systems, relying on static Knowledge Bases (KBs), our proposal addresses settings where the KB is initially empty and is progressively populated through human decisions. The system stores previous decisions as retrievable precedents and moves from silent observation to evidence-grounded contestation and, finally, to autonomous handling with abstention. Against an independent baseline, iRAG matches final-decision error under 10% drift without retrieval decay and reduces it under 40% drift across all configurations. Retrieval decay improves performance on changed knowledge while increasing error on stable knowledge, evidencing a stability--plasticity trade-off rather than a general advantage. Human oversight is an architectural provision of the workflow; its usability with real human users remains to be evaluated.

papers.title: perturber: A Stateless Service for Semantics-Preserving Text Perturbations
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) evaluations on clean benchmarks overstate model robustness: real inputs arrive perturbed, and these meaning-preserving variants routinely move model answers. Studying this systematically requires applying perturbations one at a time, reproducibly, and identically wherever they run, yet existing tools couple them to a benchmarking stack rather than packaging them as a reusable transform layer. We present perturber, a stateless service and Python library that applies exactly one semantics-preserving perturbation per call, drawn from a first-party catalog of 68 perturbations across 11 families. It turns on a single primitive, with composition left to the caller chaining calls, so the service and the library produce identical output by construction. We evaluate the tool itself, its correctness, reproducibility, and cost, rather than any model's robustness, measuring meaning-preservation per perturbation rather than assuming it. The demonstration adds a live playground, an introspectable catalog for benchmark selection, and a one-command reproducible evaluation.

papers.title: Recurrent Harness for Agentic Continual Learning
papers.abstract: Language model agents increasingly operate over long interaction streams, requiring online adaptation to distribution shifts through continual learning. However, existing agent harnesses typically either evolve their states only through forward information flow or rely on additional replay or validation data for harness optimization. To address this, we propose ReHarness, a recurrent harness framework for agentic continual learning that complements forward read and write with backward revision under a strictly online streaming protocol. We ask what information could have been captured differently in the harness state to better inform the current instance in the stream. Specifically, after each instance, we leverage the resulting trajectory as feedback to revise the reflections retrieved for that instance, thereby propagating feedback backward through the textual harness state. Across three continual learning benchmarks and three language model backbones, ReHarness consistently outperforms strong raw-context baselines, memory- and reflection-based methods, and prompt optimization approaches. Further analysis shows that ReHarness produces source-grounded and meaningful revisions, corrects overgeneralized or outdated experience under distribution shifts, and improves both stability and plasticity during continual learning.

papers.title: GeoFitBench-LLM: A Benchmark for Assessing Large Language Models' Capabilities in Geospatial Data Requirements Elicitation for Geo-Analytic Tasks
papers.abstract: Large language models are becoming central to GeoAI systems, yet their evaluation rarely considers the elicitation of geospatial data requirements. This omission is critical as retrieval oriented geo-analytic tasks cannot be supported reliably without first identifying the necessary datasets and constraints. GeoFitBench-LLM is introduced as a benchmark for assessing whether LLMs can infer the datasets, the supporting resources and the constraints required by geo-analytic requests in natural language. The benchmark is structured around two reasoning dimensions, Spatio-Temporal Relational and Semantic Grounding, reflecting long-standing challenges in geospatial information retrieval and related natural language tasks. Ground truth requirements are encoded in a fixed, provider-independent schema for reproducible evaluation of resource identification and attribute-level specification. Experiments on seven models under minimal prompting indicate that identifying the necessary resources is often achievable, with GPT-5.4 Thinking achieving the best result by recovering the complete set of resources in 66.67% of benchmark requests. Results further indicate that accurate fitness-for-use specification remains more difficult as inferential demands increase.

papers.title: Robust and Scalable UAV-UGV Planning for Aerial Monitoring under Energy and Precedence Constraints
papers.abstract: We consider planning for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and unmanned ground vehicle (UGV) teams in aerial monitoring missions with ordering requirements on the monitoring points to be visited by the UAV. The system consists of multiple UAV-UGV teams, each comprising one UAV and one UGV. UAV energy limitations are modeled through endurance, defined as the maximum flight time on a full battery. The UGVs serve as mobile charging stations and transport the UAVs between consecutive aerial tours. Given a set of monitoring points subject to ordering constraints and the teams' initial and terminal positions, the objective is to minimize mission completion time while satisfying UAV energy limits and the required visit order under bounded travel-time disturbances that may arise during execution. Unlike prior work, the plan jointly determines vehicle routes and their timing, allowing teams to slow down as needed to satisfy the ordering constraints. We develop a polynomial-time algorithm that generates efficient solutions to the underlying NP-hard planning problem. We establish feasibility guarantees, characterize the algorithm's computational complexity, and evaluate its performance via numerical comparisons.

papers.title: Topology Construction Algorithms for DECT NR+ in Normal and Ultra-Dense Deployments
papers.abstract: The 5G-grade DECT NR+ technology designed to support massive machine-type communications (mMTC) relies on the decentralized mesh connectivity concept. The currently utilized topology construction algorithms are very sensitive to the node density, which causes interference at the node association phase and may lead to instable topologies. In this study, we propose several algorithms that need to be utilized at relay and leaf nodes to allow stabilization of the topology: (i) load-dependent relay allocation, (ii) hysteresis-based association control, (iii) blacklist-based association control, and (iv) smart beacon placement. Due to the complex interference structure in DECT NR+ mesh systems, we utilize system-level simulations to assess the performance in both normal and ultra-dense conditions in terms of the efficiency of topology construction and the performance characteristics of the resulting topology. Our results show that dense DECT NR+ networks do suffer from topology instability, with reassociation rates exceeding 10 per second and recovery times lasting over 10 minutes. By implementing the proposed mechanisms, the network dynamically scales, reducing the number of required relays by more than half, from 34% to 15%. They also stabilize the topology by reducing the reassociation rates to just 2-3 per second allowing large-scale networks of several hundred nodes to operate efficiently.

papers.title: Could four-dimensional $φ^4$ theory exist beyond the usual triviality arguments?
papers.abstract: Do lattice triviality, suspected Borel non-summability and the perturbative Landau pole exclude an interacting four-dimensional theory satisfying the Osterwalder--Schrader axioms and reproducing every renormalized coefficient of positive-coupling $O(N)$ $φ^4$ theory? An example involving one real function separates vanishing cutoff limits along its allowed bare trajectories from a nonzero result obtained by renormalizing the coefficients first; an exponentially small correction preserves its expansion and removes the pole in its running coupling. For the massless two-point expansion of the singlet composite $Φ_aΦ_a$ at leading order in $1/N$, ordinary Borel summation fails even for Gaussian smearing. The arithmetic mean of two Borel integrals along opposite imaginary rays defines a real distribution on every four-dimensional Schwartz momentum or position test, with finite-order remainder bounds uniform on bounded test sets. Two alternative covariances with nonnegative mass spectral weights remove the Euclidean pole and construct generalized free fields. After a fixed contact subtraction, their Euclidean extensions preserve every coefficient of the collective correlations obtained by Wick pairing. The interacting finite-$N$ family remains open. We also state a conditional interacting route through the physical scalar correlations of a larger theory (the parent) with heavy particles. A concrete $N=1$ gauge--Higgs--fermion candidate has a tuned one-loop trajectory on which all interaction couplings tend to zero in the ultraviolet, and a stable tree vacuum with additional masses comparable to the heavy scale. Constructing the parent and its corrected ultraviolet trajectory, and proving coefficient decoupling and the exact remainder bounds as the quartic coupling tends to zero and the family's heavy masses grow, remain open.

papers.title: MindVLM: Neural-Grounded Visual Captioning via Subject-Aware Semantic Evidence Selection
papers.abstract: Translating visual brain activity into natural language offers a powerful window into human cognition and neural semantic representation. Most prior brain-captioning approaches project fMRI signals into language space using paired supervision. However, the widely used Natural Scenes Dataset (NSD) was built based only on image-fMRI pairs, while existing methods rely on MS-COCO captions as indirect textual supervision. Critically, during fMRI acquisition, participants observe only cropped image regions, whereas the associated MS-COCO captions describe full scenes. This mismatch creates a fundamental gap between neural representations and textual supervision, introducing an inherent semantic loss in NSD-based brain captioning. To mitigate this limitation, we reformulate brain captioning as Neural-Grounded Visual Captioning, where language is generated directly from visually grounded neural evidence rather than text supervision. We propose MindVLM, a framework that maps fMRI signals into subject-aware visual tokens and leverages a frozen vision language model (VLM) to produce interpretable and personalized descriptions. Instead of point-wise regression, MindVLM focuses on extracting semantically relevant visual cues from neural activity, naturally accommodating partial observability and inter-subject variability. Extensive experiments on NSD show that MindVLM consistently improves caption quality across multiple VLM backbones, including LLaVA-v1.5, Qwen2.5-VL, and Gemma3, beyond intrinsic model priors. Despite requiring neither text supervision nor an LLM during training and operating under an image-grounded inference paradigm distinct from conventional captioning methods, MindVLM remains competitive with supervised approaches, suggesting that subject-specific neural grounding provides an efficient, scalable, and interpretable path toward faithful brain-to-language generation.

papers.title: Simple Standard Errors for Complicated (Quasi-)Experimental Designs
papers.abstract: We develop standard errors for estimates of causal effects in settings where the distribution of treatment exposures is known but potentially exhibits complicated dependence patterns across units. Such dependence arises, for example, in settings with spillovers/interference across units or when the treatment assignment is spatially correlated. Our variance estimator generalizes several properties of the Neyman variance estimator for completely randomized experiments to general designs: it is unbiased for an upper bound on the variance from the design-based perspective; the conservativeness of this upper bound depends on the heterogeneity of treatment effects; and it is also valid under certain forms of super-population sampling of the potential outcomes. Our estimator reduces to standard approaches in simple designs, such as the Neyman variance estimator in completely randomized experiments and the cluster-robust variance estimator in cluster-randomized experiments. We show that the proposed estimator is admissible among the class of quadratic-form variance estimators, and derive asymptotic conditions under which it is consistent for an upper bound on the asymptotic variance of the treatment effect estimator. In simulations and applications based on two empirical studies, one with peer effects and another with a spatially correlated treatment, we find that the proposed variance estimator performs well, and in some cases yields standard errors that are 2-3 times shorter than those of existing alternatives.

papers.title: Hook algebras and determinantal varieties
papers.abstract: In characteristic zero, we prove that the Tor algebras of the generic, symmetric, and skew-symmetric determinantal rings are Koszul with respect to a natural regrading. In particular, their Eilenberg--Moore spectral sequence degenerates, which allows us to explicitly determine the Poincaré series of their residue fields and answers a problem raised by Avramov. To do this, we construct the universal hook algebra and prove that it has a quadratic Gröbner basis and thus is Koszul. This leads to a new standard monomial construction of the irreducible polynomial GL-representations, alongside the Schur and Weyl functors, which is of independent interest.

papers.title: WoodBR-Cross: A public wood-image dataset and individual-tree-disjoint benchmark for species identification
papers.abstract: Wood identification supports timber inspection and species conservation. However, benchmarks can overestimate generalization when photographs of the same tree occur in training and test sets. We present WoodBR-Cross: 4,875 transverse-surface microscope images, 38 operational taxonomic classes and 303 catalogue-linked trees. A species subset contains 3,406 images, 20 classes and 214 trees. Task A evaluates all classes using duplicate-aware image partitions. B1 partitions images of the species subset, allowing different photographs of one tree across partitions. B2 keeps each tree's photographs together, testing recognition of unseen trees on the same subset. We benchmark three backbones and baselines across three folds and five training seeds. Validation-selected ConvNeXt-Tiny achieves B2 tree-level macro-F1 of 0.8621 +/- 0.0317; frozen DINOv2 features yield 0.9000 +/- 0.0722. Values are means +/- SD across three folds; fine-tuned scores are seed-averaged within folds. This resource supports reproducible, group-aware evaluation.

papers.title: The GAPS programme at TNG LXXXII. The first atmospheric investigation of the gas giant WASP-13b at high resolution with GIARPS
papers.abstract: Low-density transiting gas giant exoplanets are key benchmarks for atmospheric studies. Despite their large-scale heights, many of them remain poorly characterised. We present the first atmospheric investigation at high-resolution of the inflated (R$_\mathrm{p}$$\sim$1.4 R$_{\mathrm{J}}$), hot Jupiter (T$\sim$1500$ \mathrm{K}$) WASP-13 b aiming at constraining its atmospheric composition and refine its orbital geometry. We analysed four transits observed with GIARPS at the TNG. Updated stellar and planetary parameters were re-derived from the most precise literature values, and a new Rossiter-McLaughlin analysis was performed to measure the projected spin-orbit angle ($λ$) and stellar rotational velocity ($v\sin{i_\star}$). Atmospheric signals were searched using high-resolution spectroscopy, both with cross-correlation and single-line analyses, targeting key atomic and molecular species (e.g. \ion{He}{I}, H$α$, \ion{Na}{I}, H$_2$O, CO). We find a well-aligned orbit ($λ$ = 2.7$\pm$1.1$^\circ$) and $v\sin{i_\star}$ = 4.5$\pm$0.1 km s$^{-1}$, improving upon previous constraints. No significant atmospheric absorption is detected in either VIS or NIR data. Injection-and-recovery tests exclude an isothermal atmosphere with metallicity [M/H]$\lesssim$10$\times$[M/H]$_\odot$ and simultaneously a grey cloud top pressure P$_{\rm cloud}\gtrsim10$ mbar, under the assumption of chemical equilibrium. WASP-13 b appears to belong to the class of low-density hot Jupiters with weak or featureless transmission spectra, most likely shaped by the presence of high-altitude clouds. Although a highly metal-enriched atmosphere cannot be fully excluded, current evidence disfavours this scenario. Further observations with next-generation facilities will be essential to characterise the atmospheric properties of this challenging target.

papers.title: Symmetric, rational and infinitely many $(23_4)$ configurations, and the end of the existence problem for geometric $(n_4)$ configurations
papers.abstract: A geometric $(n_4)$ configuration is a set of $n$ points and $n$ lines in the real projective plane such that every point lies on exactly four of the lines and every line contains exactly four of the points. The question of which $n$ admit such a configuration was posed by Grünbaum in 2000, and successive work of Bokowski, Grünbaum, Schewe, Pilaud and Cuntz settled every case but $n=23$. We settle this last case by bounding the symmetry of such configurations and classifying the most symmetric ones exactly. We prove that for every prime $n\equiv3\pmod4$ the group of projective symmetries of a geometric $(n_4)$ configuration has order at most four, explaining why symmetric constructions failed at $n=23$, and the same argument bounds the symmetry of $(n_5)$ configurations for primes $n\not\equiv1\pmod5$. Reducing the Klein four-group case to 4021 bilinear polynomial systems and solving all of them exactly with Gröbner bases, we show that exactly two $(23_4)$ configurations reach this bound up to projective equivalence and that there are no others even over $\mathbb{C}$. Both are self-polar; the first has integer coordinates and the second is defined over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{17})$ but not over $\mathbb{Q}$. Consequently geometric $(n_4)$ configurations exist if and only if $n\ge18$ and $n\ne19$. The same classification recovers Cuntz's $(22_4)$ and $(26_4)$ configurations and finds three new combinatorial types at $n=22$ and $94$ at $n=26$. Among self-polar $(23_4)$ configurations with a single involution we find $50$ more, defined over number fields of degree at most $7$. Four of them deform in one-parameter families, and computing three of these exactly, one birational to the modular curve $X_1(11)$, we prove that there are infinitely many geometric $(23_4)$ configurations, among them infinitely many with rational coordinates that are self-polar and have no projective symmetry.

papers.title: Limit theorems for random matrix products with a simple top Lyapunov exponent
papers.abstract: We study products of independent, identically distributed random matrices with an exponential moment and a simple top Lyapunov exponent, without assuming irreducibility. Outside an exceptional invariant subspace called the equator, we establish contraction on average for a weighted projective distance and a spectral gap for the associated Markov operator. We obtain a central limit theorem, a Berry--Esseen bound, deviation estimates near the mean, and an almost sure invariance principle both for the growth of a fixed vector outside the equator and for the operator norm. For fixed vectors, a non-arithmeticity assumption also yields a local limit theorem and a renewal theorem. Our contraction criterion applies more generally to mostly contracting random maps on locally compact spaces with a Lyapunov function, including certain random interval maps.

papers.title: Amortised Inference through One-Step Implicit Sampling
papers.abstract: Efficient sampling from Bayesian posterior distributions in high dimensions remains a hard problem, despite advances in theory and algorithms. Multiple steps are usually required to draw unbiased samples, for example, iterations of an MCMC algorithm or integration steps in a diffusion-based amortised sampler. However, scalable one-step amortised inference remains a challenging open problem. In this work, we build upon recent progress in data-driven generative modelling to offer a possible solution for one-step amortised sampling. Our one-step implicit sampler (OSIS) uses short-time MCMC dynamics to define a local target for the evolution of an implicitly modelled distribution. In the asymptotic limit, the modelled distribution is a fixed point of the MCMC kernel and thus samples from the target. We analyse the convergence properties of OSIS and show connections with other generative modelling and sampling algorithms. We study various design choices and show that OSIS performs well compared to multi-step amortised samplers and non-amortised MCMC baselines while being far more efficient at sampling time.

papers.title: Expert-level detection of low-voltage intervals in EEG as a robust biomarker of neonatal encephalopathy
papers.abstract: Background: Discontinuity in neonatal EEG is a critical marker of brain dysfunction but can be difficult to quantify visually. Inter-burst intervals (IBIs) are a key characteristic of discontinuity, yet their definition does not easily translate to AI detection. Objectives: To introduce low-voltage intervals (LVIs), defined exclusively by amplitude and duration, as a context-independent alternative to IBIs, develop an AI detection method for LVIs, and assess their clinical utility as a marker of brain injury. Methods: We developed a ConvNeXt model to detect LVIs and compared its performance with existing methods. We then tested the clinical relevance of detected LVIs across four applications: 1) grading background EEG abnormalities on an open benchmark dataset, 2) classifying clinical hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy (HIE) grades and comparing with a normal EEG dataset, 3) seizure prediction, and 4) association with seizure burden. Results: For training and validation, 654 hours of per-channel EEG from 123 neonates were reviewed and 51,162 LVIs were annotated. On held-out validation, ConvNeXt had an AUC of 0.996 and a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.926. Model-reader agreement exceeded inter-reader agreement ($Δκ= 0.025$, 95% CI: 0.007 to 0.045, $p<0.001$), attaining expert-level equivalence. On a combined dataset of 444 neonates, percentage LVI showed a strong association with EEG grades (Spearman's $ρ=0.801$), a moderate association with HIE grades ($ρ=0.384$), a weaker association with seizure burden ($ρ=0.244$), and a strong seizure prediction capacity (AUC $=0.872$). Conclusion: AI detection of LVIs achieves expert-level equivalence, whereas quantitative features do not. Automated LVI quantification provides a robust clinical biomarker of neonatal encephalopathy associated with background EEG activity, HIE severity, and seizure risk.

papers.title: The square function estimate for the cone in four dimensions
papers.abstract: We obtain the $L^3$ reverse square function estimate for the light cone in four dimensions from the critical local-smoothing and round-cone propagation statements in the September 2026 OpenAI manuscript. We state these inputs, together with the plate maximal theorem of Di Plinio and Parissis, in a preliminaries section. The proof passes from geometric concentration of packet coefficients to regularity of the analyzed wave, and then from free waves to arbitrary functions supported near the cone. As a consequence, we obtain the corresponding $L^3$ estimate for the sphere and elliptic paraboloids in three dimensions.

papers.title: A Framework for Arbitrary-Order Electromagnetic Field Approximation Based on Analytical Solutions of Maxwell's Equations
papers.abstract: The standard Yee finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) algorithm uses Maxwell's equations to replace first order temporal derivatives with spatial curls. In this work, the relation is extended to arbitrary orders: a Time-Space Theorem establishes the correspondence between higher-order temporal derivatives and successively higher-order spatial curl operators. Based on this relation, an arbitrary-order framework for electromagnetic field approximations is developed. The framework constructs higher temporal orders through higher curl orders and permits different spatial discretizations and curl-estimation techniques, thereby providing a general basis for developing numerical algorithms of arbitrary orders. As one implementation, an arbitrary-order FDTD algorithm is constructed using staggered time and space stepping together with recursive curl estimations. Numerical simulations of an initial-value problem are performed for temporal approximation orders from second to tenth order while the spatial and temporal step sizes are kept fixed. Comparisons with the analytical solution show that the errors decrease rapidly and monotonically with increasing approximation order. These results demonstrate the practical potential of the framework for high-accuracy electromagnetic computation and provide a basis for further development of arbitrary-order numerical methods.

papers.title: Digraph Laplacian spectra: The 2005 polygon conjecture fails for all orders above four
papers.abstract: Let $Λ_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of standardized Laplacian matrices of order $n$, equivalently, of stochastic $n\times n$ matrices with off-diagonal entries at most $\frac1n$. In 2005, a polygon $S_n\subseteqΛ_n$ was constructed, and it was conjectured that $Λ_n=S_n$; this holds for $n\le3$. We show that the conjecture fails for every $n\ge5$. The vertices of $S_n$ are eigenvalues of circulant Laplacians built from powers of the directed $n$-cycle. To first order, no perturbation of these circulants moves such an eigenvalue out of $S_n$; however, adding chords with nonconstant weights moves it along an edge of $S_n$ to first order and, with an explicit coefficient, beyond the supporting line of this edge to second order. Consequently, every edge of $S_n$ not incident to $0$ or $1$ contains interior points of $Λ_n$, except possibly, for even $n$, the two horizontal edges, whereas the four edges incident to $0$ or $1$ lie on $\partialΛ_n$. For $n=4$, whose only other edges are horizontal, the question was left open in the previous versions; it has since been settled, $Λ_4=S_4$, by a computer-assisted proof of L. Marshall, after an earlier claim by D.Z. Liu, who also proved that $Λ_n$ is not convex for $n\ge5$. We certify an explicit weighted counterexample for $n=5$, lying only $1.5\cdot10^{-3}$ outside $S_5$, and an unweighted one for $n=7$: the directed $6$-cycle with a duplicated vertex. Its eigenvalue outside $S_7$ is also an eigenvalue of the two-chord digraph that ends the above perturbation; for the analogous digraphs of order $n$, the excess is asymptotic to $\frac{π^2}{2n^4}$. We also observe that $S_n$ is a zonotope, describe $Λ_n$ in terms of eigenvectors, and prove that $S_m\subseteq S_n$ whenever $m\mid n$.

papers.title: Nef Hattori classes and products of projective lines
papers.abstract: Let \(X\) be a smooth connected complex projective variety with an effective algebraic \(\mathbb C^{\times}\)-action, a nonempty finite fixed locus whose weights are \(\pm1\). We show that if its Hattori line bundles are nef, then \(X\) is algebraically isomorphic to \((\mathbb{P}^1)^{\dim X}\), and these bundles become the hyperplane bundles of the factors. The product statement follows from the nef-complexity classification of Enwright and collaborators, and we describe the isomorphism through global sections. To test the required nefness we specialise the orbit-graph criterion of Romano and Wiśniewski. The Hirzebruch surface \(\mathbb F_2\) is an example why the topological hypotheses alone do not imply either the product conclusion or the Fano property.

papers.title: Non-Prehensile Multi-Object Placement with Mobile Robots via Diffusion-Based Trajectory Planning
papers.abstract: Non-prehensile manipulation with mobile robots has primarily targeted placement in coarse goal regions. Precision placement has been studied with manipulators on benchmarks such as Push-T, where an omnidirectional end effector can readily re-approach an object from any side. For a mobile robot, correcting the same placement errors may require wide repositioning maneuvers around the object. We formalize multi-object pushing with a mobile robot as a multi-target assignment problem at tight tolerances. We propose a diffusion planner with a causal factorization: each robot denoising step is followed by an object step conditioned on the current clean robot estimate. This factorization allows us to sample multiple object outcomes for a single robot plan, capturing the multi-modality of pushing. We also design a set of pushing-specific costs for mobile robots, used for both guidance and best-of-$N$ sampling at inference. On Push-T, our planner attains the highest success rate of the methods we compare, while having the lowest rate of implausible object motion. Across three multi-box pushing environments resembling warehouse scenarios, it raises the fraction of boxes placed by $21.5$ percentage points over an unguided baseline, and replans $1.8\times$ faster than a planner that denoises the two trajectories together. Lastly, we deploy the guided planner on a TurtleBot 3 Burger with object shapes absent from the training data, where it places $85.0\%$ of objects within tolerance against Diffusion Policy's $37.5\%$.

papers.title: Fast computational primitives for La-cross qLDPC codes
papers.abstract: Quantum LDPC codes promise to reduce the overhead of fault-tolerant quantum computation, but their practical use requires efficient logical gates, measurements, and access to non-Clifford resources. Here, we develop a complete set of computational primitives for La-cross hypergraph product codes. For a subclass of these codes, we show that seed automorphisms together with fold-transversal gates generate the full logical Clifford group up to Pauli corrections. We further prove that every rank one logical operator admits $D$ pairwise disjoint physical representatives, enabling parallel gauging and a space--time tradeoff for logical measurements. Finally, we construct an addressable surface code interface for injecting externally prepared resource states into selected logical qubits. Together, these results establish La-cross codes as a simple, low-connectivity generalisation of surface code computation, retaining analogous computational primitives while providing a complete Clifford+$T$ instruction set across multiple encoded qubits.

papers.title: Multistatic Terahertz ISAC for Object Shape Identification
papers.abstract: 6G networks are expected to sense their surroundings using the same waveforms that carry data. We ask how much can be learned about the shape of an object from the terahertz echoes that user equipment transmissions produce as they scatter from that object on their way to a ceiling-mounted access point, with no sensing hardware beyond the communication link itself. We build a physics-based multistatic forward model at a 300 GHz carrier with 50 GHz of bandwidth, combining Physical Optics (PO) and Physical Theory of Diffraction (PTD) scattering with an image-source multipath lattice, molecular absorption and directional horn antennas. The model makes explicit a property of the PO mechanism hierarchy that is usually left implicit. Six physically distinct mechanisms share only three frequency exponents, so the spectral slope does not by itself determine which mechanisms a target presents and therefore cannot by itself determine its geometry. Angular diversity is accordingly a requirement for identifiability rather than an optional refinement. We compare a transmitter-count-invariant 2D-CNN with a physics-informed RBF-SVM on object orientations never seen in training. Accuracy climbs from roughly 70 percent with one transmitter to 96-97 percent with 20. The CNN gains in two regimes, irregular placement and lossy targets, while on metal under quasi-uniform placement the SVM baseline is fully competitive. Performance falls off gradually under occlusion, holding 78 percent with three quarters of the surface hidden and 63 percent when the classifier has never seen an occluded target. Multi-object scenes are limited by interference between overlapping returns rather than by angular coverage, so presence detection saturates after roughly four transmitters.

papers.title: Theory of Disorder-Induced Multimode Coupling in a Fabry-Pérot Cavity
papers.abstract: Strong light--matter interactions have attracted significant interest in physical chemistry due to the potential for modifying molecular processes by hybridizing with cavity photons and forming polaritonic states. However, for a disordered molecular ensemble within an optical cavity capable of supporting multiple photon modes, theoretical understanding of multimode polaritons remains incomplete, particularly regarding whether and how distinct photon modes are mutually coupled through molecules. In this work, we generalize the collective mode expansion formalism to incorporate multiple photonic modes and show that spatial and orientational disorder in the light--matter coupling strength (originating from dipole orientation fluctuations and photonic field inhomogeneity) can mediate cross-mode coupling. This disorder-induced coupling allows for energy transfer to otherwise unexcited photon modes through a mechanism termed disorder-induced multimode activation (DIMA). Using an effective one-dimensional Fabry--Pérot cavity as a test system, we demonstrate that the cross-mode energy transfer through DIMA can be controlled by changing the molecular layer thickness and the optical properties of the mirrors. Furthermore, we show that DIMA is robust against weak energetic disorder. This mechanistic understanding lays the foundation for a systematic control of multimode photon coupling using disorder-induced effects.

papers.title: Predictive-Context LOO: Bayesian Model Comparison with Pretrained Predictive Learners
papers.abstract: Leave-one-out (LOO) cross-validation, a standard tool for Bayesian model assessment, evaluates each observation using a LOO predictive distribution derived from the model itself. In this work, we introduce an alternative construction in which posterior predictive simulation connects the Bayesian model to an external pretrained predictive learner. Our method, Predictive-Context LOO (PC-LOO), fits a Bayesian model once, generates posterior-predictive synthetic data, and uses them as context for the learner to approximate each LOO predictive density. Under an oracle construction, averaging contexts generated from the LOO posterior recovers the exact LOO predictive density. Practical PC-LOO replaces the oracle predictor by the pretrained learner and the LOO posterior by the full posterior. We quantify these errors through learner compatibility $C_i$ and deletion influence $V_i$, obtaining $H^2 (p^{LOO}_{i} , q^{PC}_{i}) \leq C_{i} + V_{i}$. The identity also holds for any fixed subset of $M$ context points, allowing $M \ll n - 1$ as the learner's context budget, and scalability to large datasets. Experiments with TabICL support this decomposition, deletion influence decays approximately as $n^{-1}$, while learner compatibility can remain limiting at large $n$. PC-LOO remains accurate with reduced context sizes, while model comparison accuracy is governed by differences in approximation error across models rather than their absolute errors. More broadly, PC-LOO establishes posterior predictive simulation as a principled interface for integrating pretrained predictive learners into Bayesian workflows.

papers.title: Fin_Agent at FinEval 2026: Task-Aware Methods for Multilingual Financial NLP
papers.abstract: We present Fin_Agent, our submission to the FinEval 2026 shared task on multilingual fi nancial language understanding. Our sys tems address Greek financial named-entity recognition, Japanese implicit communication recognition, and multilingual financial ques tion answering. For Greek NER, we com bine annotation-aware numeric rules with zero shot Qwen2.5-32B classification, achieving 0.9521 public F1 and 0.8884 private F1. For Japanese implicit communication, an inter pretable cue-based ordinal scorer achieves 98.0% test accuracy. For multilingual financial QA, BGE-M3retrieval with Qwen3-32B gen eration achieves 0.3023 and 0.3419 ROUGE-1 F1 on the public and private splits. Key limita tions include dataset-specific rules, handcrafted cues, and limited supervision. Implementa tion code is available https://github.com/ Rashidnira/finagent-fineval-2026.

papers.title: An exact Delaunay flux identity for compact equilibria in the liquid drop model
papers.abstract: We revisit the construction of compact liquid drop equilibria from Delaunay unduloids in [Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 249 (2025), Paper No. 74]. We evaluate exactly the coefficient arising in the final solvability condition of the Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction, identifying it as the product of the axial period and the normalised Delaunay flux. Using this identity and the monotonicity of the period, we establish the conjectured positivity of the coefficient and prove that its product with the period strictly increases with the neck radius. We also derive an exact relation between the volume and the surface area of one period and prove that both strictly decrease with the neck radius. These results extend the construction throughout the embedded unduloid family and yield compact equilibria of every sufficiently large mass, with reference neck radii converging to any prescribed interior value as the mass tends to infinity.

papers.title: Reconstruction of Finite Posets of Width Three
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite ordered set of width at most three and cardinality at least four is reconstructible from its deck. This settles the width-three part of an open problem posed by Schröder in Ordered Sets; the separate question concerning ordered sets of height one is not addressed here. The new ingredient is a criterion for recovering the marked maximal deck of an ordered set with exactly three maximal elements from its unmarked maximal deck and the isomorphism type of the suborder obtained by deleting all maximal elements. We express the criterion as an orbital balance condition on the attachment ideals in this common base. Necessity follows by double counting; sufficiency uses the structure of automorphism actions in width at most three. The full-deck theorem then follows from reconstruction results of Schröder concerning maximal cards and marked maximal cards. A local reattachment argument correcting one intermediate step in the two-maximal-element case is included in an appendix.

papers.title: Hankel Matrix Decompositions and Digital Sequences over Function Fields
papers.abstract: This paper studies formal Laurent series, with particular emphasis on their continued-fraction and Laurent-series expansions. Knowledge of both expansions is important, for example, in the study of Kronecker-type sequences in uniform distribution theory and in the search for potential counterexamples to variants of Littlewood's conjecture over fields of formal Laurent series. Our approach investigates Hankel matrices over a field and relates them to Laurent-series expansions over the same field. We describe such matrices via a block $\mathcal{L}\mathcal{B}\mathcal{U}$ decomposition, using recursive algorithms based on the continued-fraction coefficients of the corresponding Laurent series. The upper-triangular factor $\mathcal{U}$ has several remarkable properties. In particular, it is constructed columnwise from the so-called Ostrowski-type representations of powers of $X$. Applying $\mathcal{U}$ in Niederreiter's digital construction yields an Ostrowski-type van der Corput sequence that can be related to the corresponding Kronecker-type sequence. For ordinary Kronecker sequences, such a relation is known in only one case, that of the $(n\varphi)$-sequence. The original motivation for our study of Hankel matrices was to recast the search for counterexamples to variants of Littlewood's conjecture over fields of Laurent series as the search for specific Kronecker-type sequences. Interestingly, the method developed for the study of Kronecker-type sequences also allows a new perspective on the celebrated Sobol' construction. Our approach yields a short and elegant proof of its excellent distribution properties.

papers.title: Distributed Datalog at Scale with Worst-Case Optimal Joins
papers.abstract: Scalable logic-based analytics are frequently dominated by cyclic multi-way joins over large relational datasets. State-of-the-art systems evaluate these joins through chains of binary joins, incurring substantial overhead from large intermediate relations that must be materialized and redistributed across the network. Worst-Case Optimal Joins (WCOJ) offer a provably superior alternative by evaluating joins one variable at a time, eliminating intermediate blowup. However, existing WCOJ implementations target either shared-memory machines or one-shot, non-recursive queries on dataflow and big-data platforms, leaving WCOJ-based recursive evaluation on distributed-memory HPC systems an open problem. We present, to our knowledge, the first distributed-memory Datalog engine that uses WCOJ for recursive fixpoint evaluation. Our design builds on HyperCube partitioning, which hash-partitions relations along variable-aligned grid dimensions and replicates them along missing dimensions, and extends it from a single shuffle to iterative execution: in every semi-naive iteration, only newly derived tuples are repartitioned and re-replicated, using MPI all-to-all collectives and per-dimension all-gathers over subcube communicators, while the same layout is reused across iterations so that all WCOJ intersections remain rank-local. We evaluate our system on the Aurora and Polaris leadership-class supercomputers at Argonne National Laboratory using graph mining and program analysis benchmarks, demonstrating strong scalability, outperforming state-of-the-art Datalog engines on most benchmarks, and characterizing how partition dimensionality trades runtime against memory feasibility.

papers.title: Lightweight Systems for Spatial Semantic Segmentation of Sound Scenes
papers.abstract: Spatial semantic segmentation of sound scenes (S5) jointly performs audio source separation and tagging on a multichannel audio mixture. Therefore, an S5 system can be decomposed into an audio tagging model and a separation model. The baseline S5 system in task~4 of the DCASE 2025 challenge uses M2D and ResUNet models for tagging and separation, respectively. These are large in overall size and therefore not appropriate for use in embedded devices. The main aim of this paper is to assess the performance loss in an S5 system when using lightweight tagging and separation models instead. To this end, we first compare the tagging performance of lightweight audio tagging models, namely PANNs and DyMNs, in terms of label prediction accuracy against the baseline M2D model. Secondly, we assess separation performance in terms of the scale-invariant signal-to-distortion ratio of the baseline ResUNet separator relative to that of a convolutional-based separator using SuDoRMRF. Finally, we combine the tagging and separation models across various configurations and assess the overall performance of the S5 system using the class-aware signal-to-distortion ratio.

papers.title: Critical Mass: Structure-Disjoint Splits Drift With the Libraries They Are Built On
papers.abstract: Molecular machine learning evaluates out-of-distribution performance with structure disjoint splits, a construction rule fixed once at the scale its library happened to have: threshold a pairwise distance, then assign whole connected components to folds. For predicting structures from mass spectra, the field has converged on single-linkage clustering under the myopic Maximum Common Edge Subgraph (MCES) distance at a threshold of 10. This convention was set on 29,000 molecules but public libraries now hold 227,690 molecules. MCES is NP-hard per pair over a quadratically growing set, and so the criterion has never been evaluated at that scale. We propose an optimized version of this criterion, allowing for computationally feasible application on the public libraries: Admissible bounds and a union-find skip reduce $2.6 \times 10^{10}$ molecular pairs to only $1.15 \times 10^{7}$ integer programs, a $2{,}259\times$ saving, while provably producing the lossless partition. We find that at this scale the graph percolates. A single component holds $95.5\%$ of the library, capping any test set at $4.5\%$. What remains is not merely smaller, but systematically different: a held-out compound outweighs a training compound 88.1\% of the time, because a fixed absolute budget is a tighter relative tolerance on a larger molecule. Large library benchmarks using this splitting rule naively therefore conflate structural novelty with extrapolation to larger, more complex chemistry.

papers.title: Enabling Extended SGX Enclaves inside Confidential Virtual Machines
papers.abstract: Confidential Virtual Machines (CVMs), such as AMD SEV-SNP, and process enclaves, such as Intel SGX, provide workload protection against cloud threats. However, they strongly differ in TCB, deployment cost and speed, peer workload protection, resource sharing, fine-grained isolation and attestation, and programming capabilities. Nesting process enclaves within CVMs offers an optimal solution and an opportunity to address long-standing SGX limitations: lack of intra-enclave protection, expensive transitions and exception paths, slow enclave cloning, and a restricted programming model that limits Library Operating Systems (LibOS). This paper introduces TEEVisor, a CVM-resident architecture consisting of a security monitor and a kernel driver that leverages AMD SEV-SNP Virtual Machine Privilege Levels (VMPLs) to build hardware-protected, process-level enclaves inside a guest CVM with two modes: (1) an SGX binary compatibility mode to run unmodified SGX applications; and (2) a novel extended SGX~(eSGX) mode optimizing slow execution paths and offering richer enclave programming capabilities. On commercial AMD EPYC hardware, against native CVM execution, TEEVisor incurs under 5% overhead on compute- and memory-bound workloads, around 12% on I/O-heavy applications, and accelerates enclave cloning to a rate of 93~$μ$s/MB of enclave size, demonstrating that eSGX semantics inside a CVM are practical for production use.

papers.title: Spa-Bench: A Real-Robot Benchmark for Spatial Grounding in Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) offer a promising route toward general-purpose robotics by transferring semantic knowledge from large-scale vision-language pretraining into language-conditioned control. However, most VLA evaluations emphasize aggregate manipulation success under changes in objects, instructions, or environments, leaving unclear how reliably these policies ground spatial descriptions in the physical scenes where they act. We therefore ask a sharper question: how reliably can current VLAs translate spatial descriptions into appropriate real-robot behavior? To investigate this, we introduce Spa-Bench, a real-robot benchmark that evaluates spatial grounding across six tabletop tasks covering Object State, Relative Size, Referential Description, Relational Placement, Ordinal Position, and Counting. Our primary evaluation compares in-distribution (ID) and out-of-distribution (OOD) spatial configurations while retaining training support for the relevant objects, concepts, and actions, reducing object and motor unfamiliarity as alternative explanations for failure. Four diagnostic conditions further probe physical execution, sensitivity to wording, object-task associations, and recognition that no action is required. We release 4,092 episodes collected on the SO-101 robot arm: 1,200 human-teleoperated demonstrations and 2,892 real-robot evaluation rollouts from five state-of-the-art VLA policies. Across the three fully evaluated policies, success falls from 67.5-73.3% on ID spatial configurations to 40.7-52.0% on OOD spatial configurations, while matched direct instructions improve success by 28.3-40.0 percentage points. These results show that the evaluated VLAs can often execute the required manipulations but lack robust spatial grounding. Project materials, including videos, code, and benchmark data, are available at https://justintiensmith.github.io/Spa-Bench/.

papers.title: Toward Maximizing Algebraic Connectivity via Density-Dependent Backbone Construction and Reinforcement Learning Completion
papers.abstract: This paper studies an open network design problem of constructing graph topologies with maximum algebraic connectivity under fixed numbers of vertices and edges. A density-dependent approach is proposed that decomposes the design task into two stages: a high-quality, low-cost structural backbone construction and a reinforcement learning completion stage. The method selects the backbone based on density, using complete multipartite graphs in dense regimes and Cayley graphs in low-to-intermediate regimes, and then refines the remaining edges through a learning-based procedure. Numerical results show that the proposed method achieves high algebraic connectivity with favorable runtime scalability, outperforming existing methods. These results support a structural-family-first strategy for scalable network design.

papers.title: Pointwise Hölder continuity of Lyapunov exponents of random matrix products
papers.abstract: We prove that if the first Lyapunov exponent of a compactly supported random matrix product is simple, then it is pointwise Hölder continuous for the Wasserstein--Hausdorff distance. By passing to exterior powers, we obtain pointwise Hölder continuity of the first $k$ exponents whenever they are simple.

papers.title: Primal-Dual Flow Matching for Sample-Wise Constrained Generation
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of learning to generate data while satisfying a prescribed \emph{sample-wise} constraint with a user-specified probability of constraint satisfaction. Starting with a population-level constrained negative log-likelihood minimization and using a flow-matching (FM) parameterization, under regularity assumptions and sufficient expressivity of the velocity field family, we derive guarantees on the probability of constraint satisfaction for the corresponding primal-dual optimization algorithm. We provide a practical implementation of this approach, called Primal-Dual Flow Matching (PDFM), which has direct control over constraint satisfaction rate and requires only binary membership oracle feedback for constraint satisfaction, avoiding the need for differentiable distances, projections, or special structure of the constraint set, such as convexity. We show that PDFM improves constraint satisfaction over vanilla FM and achieves competitive performance against constraint-aware baselines while maintaining distributional fidelity. Our code is available at https://github.com/ZhengyanHuan/PDFM.

papers.title: Improving the lower bound on the Laughlin gap: An SDP search
papers.abstract: A recent preprint by OpenAI resolved the spherical fermionic Laughlin spectral-gap conjecture for the full $V_1$ interaction by a Fock-space inequality: $H_Q^2\ge γH_Q$ on the lowest-Landau-level Fock space for all large flux $Q$ and every $γ$ below $0.0461673\ldots$, so that the gap above the Laughlin state at filling $1/3$ is at least $1/25$. That proof, with its original constant, has also been formalized in Lean. We show that the same argument supports a much larger constant. Two sharper estimates, a product-twirl bound for the three-body tail and a staircase price for the four-body allowance, raise the constant above $0.0601$ without changing the original certificate. Treating the auxiliary operators as the variables of a semidefinite program (SDP) and enlarging the finite set of orbital modes on which they act then gives $H_Q^2\geγH_Q$ for every $γ<γ_*=0.2190037845063196\ldots$, certified by exact rational arithmetic. Consequently the gap above the Laughlin state is at least $1/5$ for all sufficiently large spheres, and the untruncated planar $V_1$ Hamiltonian has positive spectrum bounded below by $γ_*$, uniformly in particle number and angular momentum. A heuristic extrapolation of the SDP optima suggests that auxiliary operators of the present form can give at most about $0.222$, while exact diagonalization of finite systems places the true gap near $0.4$. A larger family of auxiliary operators could push the bound further towards the true gap, and the SDP formulation makes such families easy to test. The proof of the improvement and the SDP search were completed by the AI model Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) under the author's direction.

papers.title: Activating the Annotator: Operationalising Lived Experience in Data Annotation
papers.abstract: Perspectivist NLP has established that annotator positionality shapes labels for subjective tasks, but the field still lacks methods for operationalising it. Positionality is typically operationalised as a demographic form completed at recruitment: a static attribute recorded once and treated as a covariate, on the assumption that the knowledge it indexes is active when the annotator reads an item. This paper treats that assumption as a design problem and asks whether lived experience can instead be primed by the task itself. We introduce AXLE, a pre-annotation stage in which a scenario vignette anchors a short, axis-guided conversation that is synthesised into a first-person micro-narrative and returned to the annotator before labelling begins. In a 2x2 between-subjects study (104 annotators, 30 items, 1,040 annotations) on ambiguous hate speech spanning immigration, religion and gender, elicitation was associated with higher identity resonance and higher sensitivity to harm. It also increased label entropy and lowered inter-annotator agreement: the stage appears to surface plurality rather than manufacture consensus, which distinguishes it from annotator training, whose success criterion is convergence.

papers.title: Product Monte Carlo: Expectation Under a Product of Densities
papers.abstract: Aggregating independently computed sub-sample inferences is a well-known challenge in large-scale Bayesian computation, federated learning, and opinion pooling. The core problem is to approximate a distribution whose density is proportional to a product of individual densities. We propose Product Monte Carlo (PMC), an algorithm for computing arbitrary expectations under a product of densities using only Monte Carlo draws from individual densities. We turn the intractable product expectation into a regression problem by expressing it through a family of computable conditional expectations. Besides the point estimate, our fully Bayesian regression formulation provides coherent uncertainty quantification and principled diagnostics. We establish theoretical guarantees on consistency and characterize convergence rates for the PMC estimator. Across simulated and real-data experiments varying the number, dimensionality, and heterogeneity of the component distributions, PMC achieves higher estimation accuracy, better-calibrated uncertainty coverage, and improved scalability at a lower computational cost than existing methods. In addition, PMC requires no density evaluation, making it applicable to simulation-based inference, as we demonstrate in an application with protein images.

papers.title: Bridging Human and Model Attention: Explainability Analysis of CNN, Mamba, and ViT Architectures with Gaze-Based Validation
papers.abstract: High-risk applications of deep learning require precise characterization of model decision-making. We conduct a systematic explainability evaluation across Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Vision Transformers (ViTs), and Vision Mamba (ViM). Unlike predominantly qualitative studies, we quantify the alignment between model attention and human visual perception using eye-tracking ground truth. We formalize this comparison via a standardized normalization pipeline mapping post-hoc attribution maps and gaze heatmaps onto spatial probability distributions. Alignment is evaluated across fine-grained classification, medical imaging, and emotion recognition using architecture-specific XAI methods. We measure fidelity using Jensen-Shannon similarity, Chi-square similarity, and Pearson correlation, three complementary estimators capturing support overlap, mass discrepancy, and structural co-variation. Our results reveal distinct attention dynamics: CNNs tend to exhibit a more global focus, with spatially more diffuse saliency maps that correlate well with human perception in general contexts, while ViTs demonstrate fine-grained, patch-level attention, often focused on discriminative microfeatures. The Mamba architecture shows biased behavior: it achieves strong explainability in medical tasks but exhibits divergent intensity distributions in natural images; our analytical characterization of the metrics makes this dissociation explicit, since near-unit support overlap is attained simultaneously with a vanishing linear correlation. We further analyze the effect of backbone freezing and ensemble strategies on model interpretability. The results highlight how architectural and training choices influence the alignment between model saliency and human visual attention.

papers.title: PVBRF-ID: Private, Verifiable and Byzantine-Robust Federated Intrusion Detection for Oilfield Enterprise Networks
papers.abstract: Federated learning allows dispersed oilfield sites to train a shared intrusion detector without pooling network traffic, yet its aggregation step forces a choice between privacy and robustness. Byzantine-robust rules must read each update in the clear, whereas secure aggregation hides updates from the checks that detect poisoning. We present PVBRF-ID, a two-server protocol in which sites secret-share their updates and the servers jointly test each update's norm and its cosine similarity to a reference computed on a small clean root set, revealing one accept bit per site. Commitments, Merkle roots and a homomorphic audit make the inclusion of accepted updates publicly verifiable. On a 15-class Edge-IIoTset task with ten sites holding differently distributed data and ten random seeds, PVBRF-ID matched FedAvg on clean data (macro-F1 0.708 vs. 0.706) and withstood sign-flip attacks (0.696 vs. 0.091). Against an adaptive attacker controlling 30% of sites, PVBRF-ID with secure clipping reached 0.641, whereas FedAvg fell to 0.046; plaintext multi-Krum remained higher by 0.052. An update-inference attacker recovered each site's class mix from plaintext updates (Spearman correlation 0.81) but not from one server's view. Backdoors passed the filter, and noise-based mitigation gave only heuristic protection. The implementation uses Python 3.13, NumPy 2.3, 30 rounds and 10 seeds.

papers.title: Polynomial parametrization of $\text{SL}_2$ over global function field rings
papers.abstract: We combine the universal polynomial matrix identities of Larsen--Nguyen with Trost's arithmetic lemmas to obtain polynomial parametrizations of $\text{SL}_2(\mathcal{O}_{K,S})$ for every global function field $K$ and every nonempty finite set of places $S$. The additional ingredient is a function-field cancellation lemma, proved using ray class fields and Chebotarev in odd characteristic and the perfectness of finite residue fields in characteristic two. The proof also gives a polynomial matrix over $\mathbb{Z}$ that works simultaneously for all these rings.

papers.title: AI-Driven, Timing-Aware Power Optimization
papers.abstract: Post-route power recovery changes cell choices under tightly coupled timing, electrical and physical constraints, and the value of each change depends on what it costs to repair its side effects. We propose an AI-driven framework in which a learned model drives both phases of the optimization: it ranks the powerrecovery edits to try and the repair actions that follow, while deterministic electronic design automation (EDA) analyses govern every acceptance. The framework records baseline constraint margins, identifies the damage a recovery transaction introduces in each analysis view, holds pre-existing violations at their baseline rather than working them inside the power step, and caps repair spending at a fraction of the measured saving. An ensemble of gradient-boosted models predicts power change, normalized damage reduction and constraint-regression risk from action and timing-context features available before each trial; calibrated, conservative estimates feed separate acquisition scores for recovery and repair, with a deterministic fallback when the model is uncertain. Recovery and repair remain speculative until physical implementation and fresh analysis establish baseline preservation and positive net saving. We specify the contract, the learned policy, the transactional flow and a pre-registered public evaluation protocol on open designs. Evidence from a companion study on public designs supports the contract; the learned policy is proposed, and no trained-model results or proprietary design measurements are reported.

papers.title: FallGown: A Soft Pneumatic Wearable Device for Fall Prevention
papers.abstract: Concerns about falling and potential resulting injuries prevent many older adults from participating in forms of health-improving exercise such as walking, dance, and tai chi. Existing passive devices like walkers require use of the arms for support, and active devices like exoskeletons and robotic frames are often rigid, bulky, and stigmatized, which limits their use. The FallGown is a soft wearable support structure consisting of pressurized pneumatic pouches within a fabric shell; it can support the full weight of a user's body and aims to prevent falls. It is portable (6.9 kg and 0.051 m3 when stored), minimally burdensome (7.24-20.8 N drag force depending on floor type and whether an optional rolling base frame is used), and convenient (less than 2.5 minutes on average to don and less than 0.5 minutes on average to doff). The optional rolling base lowers friction with the floor, but reduces portability and skirt deformation (which can be useful to fit through doors and other tight spaces). Fall prevention testing with a single user revealed a tradeoff between device size and stability against tipping; a skirt with 12 pneumatic pouches and a floor diameter of 1.4 meters with a base frame prevented all falls except in one case with a mechanical failure. On-board pressure sensors can sense the user's weight distribution, providing an opportunity for monitored exercise and adaptive support.

papers.title: RePrior: Measurement-Reconciled Prior Correction for Sparse-View CBCT Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Sparse-view cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is severely under-constrained by limited X-ray projections. Learned reconstruction can provide complementary anatomical information, but using it as a prior in patient-specific Gaussian reconstruction introduces two challenges. First, the discrepancy between the learned prior and current reconstruction is spatially non-uniform: some local differences contain useful missing 3D information, whereas others reflect prior bias. Second, even a volumetrically beneficial correction can conflict with the observed X-ray measurements. Since X-ray measurements are line integrals, spatially separated corrections may affect overlapping rays, with their signed projection responses reinforcing or partially canceling in the measurement residual, so their feasibility cannot always be assessed independently. In this paper, we introduce RePrior, a multi-stage progressive prior-correction framework that addresses correction actionability, measurement feasibility, and representation expressivity. Selective Correction Proposal (SCP) first identifies actionable signed local corrections from prior--reconstruction discrepancies. Measurement-Constrained Reconciliation (MCR) then jointly enforces their consistency with patient-specific X-ray measurements, while Hybrid Residual Enhancement (HRE) recovers additional correction capacity through complementary voxel- and Gaussian-domain degrees of freedom around the reconciled anchor. RePrior requires neither test-time ground truth nor case-specific network fine-tuning. RePrior gains approximately 2.6~dB in 3D PSNR over R$^2$-Gaussian across LUNA16, PANORAMA, and PENGWIN. Beyond prior-assisted reconstruction, it delivers additional gains in volumetric quality and observed-view projection fidelity, with consistent gains in held-out-view fidelity in the backbone-matched evaluation.

papers.title: Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling
papers.abstract: Vision-language reward models are trained on annotated preference pairs, which are expensive to collect, can disagree, and are ranked by benchmark accuracy. We build one with no human preference label: a linear head on an intermediate layer of a frozen Qwen3-VL backbone, trained to score a web caption above a perturbed version of the same caption; labeled data enters only to select the layer. The layer is the decisive choice, worth 5.8 points over the last layer, and one recipe transferred without re-tuning beats or at least matches GPT-4o on three benchmarks at 32B, 6.6 points ahead on VL-RewardBench, from a few thousand parameters at about a thousandth of fine-tuning compute. At an equal pair budget, perturbations teach a frozen head 3 to 5 points more than curated RLAIF-V pairs. Because the backbone is frozen, the objective is convex, and the perturbation sampler specifies the reward, which the benchmark does not identify: two heads trained on disjoint halves of the same perturbations tie on the benchmark and differ by 6.4 points in hallucination judging. Retraining the head on the policy's own verifier-labeled candidates cuts caption hallucination by 5.1 CHAIR points and lifts image-generation pass rate by 5.4, while scoring lower on every reward benchmark. Together, an intermediate-layer probe, free same-image perturbations, and a verifier-driven bootstrap turn give a recipe for multimodal reward modeling that needs no annotator, costs a fraction of fine-tuning, and is specified by the comparisons it is trained on rather than by a benchmark rank.

papers.title: Deriving Schwarzschild and Kerr from the Einstein Equivalence Principle
papers.abstract: This manuscript demonstrates that the Schwarzschild and Kerr metrics can be derived fundamentally from the Einstein Equivalence Principle (EEP) without explicit reliance on the Einstein field equations. We show that the EEP implies a gravitational stretching of length in the direction of acceleration, a spatial counterpart to time dilation. In the static case, this effect yields the constraint $g_{00}g_{11}=-1$, from which the Schwarzschild solution is recovered by taking the Newtonian limit. For the stationary case, we employ oblate spheroidal coordinates and construct a physically motivated tetrad to implement the EP, introducing gravity through three unknown functions. By applying the EEP-induced constraints and showing that the principle requires the preservation of the spacetime volume determinant ($g = g_0$), the system is reduced to a single unknown function that yields the Kerr metric. These results suggest that classical tests of General Relativity are, at their core, fundamental validations of the EEP. We further argue that the EEP leads naturally to Unimodular Gravity, implying that the existence of the cosmological constant is a direct consequence of this foundational postulate.

papers.title: Conjugate heat transfer in turbulent pipe flow with azimuthally non-uniform heating
papers.abstract: Turbulent conjugate heat transfer (CHT) in pipes with azimuthally non-uniform heating is studied theoretically and numerically with a focus on low-$\mathrm{Pr}$ fluids. While the influence of the solid properties is well documented for uniform heat flux, their effect under azimuthally non-uniform heating has not been explored systematically. We address this gap by combining spectral analysis of the problem -- which reduces arbitrary boundary conditions to a discrete set of azimuthal wavenumbers -- with well-resolved numerical simulations of thermally and hydraulically fully developed turbulent pipe flow at $\mathrm{Re}_τ\approx 180$ for $\mathrm{Pr} = \{0.025, 0.71\}$, representative of liquid metals and air. Two principal results emerge: (i) the global Nusselt number is independent of the azimuthal heat-flux distribution and exhibits only a minor dependence on the solid properties, resolving an open question for low-Prandtl-number fluids; (ii) CHT nevertheless strongly affects the azimuthally resolved mean temperature at low $\mathrm{Pr}$, where azimuthal conduction in the solid homogenises the interface heat flux, and governs the level of temperature fluctuations through the effusivity ratio (thermal activity ratio) $K$. Finally, an analysis of the turbulent Prandtl number $\mathrm{Pr}_{t}$ shows a strong anisotropy, particularly near the wall, and a dependence on the azimuthal wavenumber.

papers.title: REMM: Revisable Embodied Memory for Manipulation
papers.abstract: Long-horizon manipulation requires robots to retain task-relevant history while revising conclusions no longer supported by physical evidence. Retaining observations alone does not specify which completed conditions should be withdrawn after a disturbance or which obligations require repair. We introduce REMM, Revisable Embodied Memory for Manipulation, a supervisory memory layer for a frozen G0.5 vision-language-action executor. REMM separates an append-only evidence history from revisable task state and explicitly links derived relations and completed conditions to their supporting facts. When accepted evidence changes a supporting fact, it withdraws dependent conclusions and schedules targeted recovery at verified skill boundaries without updating the executor. Across 51 physical trials, including operator-assisted runs, REMM improves mean recorded task progress over the strongest baseline from 57% to 91% in intervention recovery and from 43% to 70% in sequence recall. Complementary video diagnostics show improved grounding of retained history into the next instruction, including comparisons with $π_{0.5}$-compatible high-level planner adaptations. These results support revisable memory as a practical interface for continued manipulation without policy retraining. Project: https://revanthsenthil.github.io/remm/.

papers.title: Byzantine-Resilient Federated Large Language Model via Hypergraph Message Passing
papers.abstract: Federated Large Language Models (FedLLMs) are promising to deliver privacy-preserving, collaborative intelligence. The decentralized training process is vulnerable to Byzantine attacks that corrupt semantic consistency and factual resilience through malicious model updates. This paper presents a new resilience strategy that prevents semantically corrupted knowledge from propagating during federated aggregation. A defense problem is formulated to jointly maximize global accuracy and suppress manipulated model updates, enabling trustworthy knowledge aggregation without accessing private local data. To strengthen the resilience of FedLLMs, we develop a novel Hypergraph Message Passing Graph Autoencoder (HMP-GAE) framework, where low-rank model updates are represented as nodes in a hypergraph and high-order semantic relationships among multiple agents are exploited through iterative message passing.
